chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the pregnant woman whose husband has died, is there expense (nafaqah) for her? He said: No. And it is reported as well that her expense is from the wealth of her child which is in her belly. He reported it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on maintenance for a pregnant widow during her waiting period?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that a pregnant widow's maintenance (nafaqah) is not drawn from her deceased husband's estate but rather from the wealth of the unborn child, reflecting the principle that the fetus is considered a dependent heir. This ruling highlights the unique status of the fetus in Shia jurisprudence as an independent entity with financial rights, distinct from the general rules of inheritance distribution. The hadith underscores the practical implication that the estate remains intact for other heirs while covering the specific needs of the pregnant widow through the child's share.
